newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Ingwe in 800 mln rand Australian coal deal.
newsitem.headline: Ingwe in 800 mln rand Australian coal deal.

text.p: Ingwe Coal Corporation Ltd has acquired 96.3 percent of Coal Mines of Australia Ltd (CMAL) in a deal worth 800 million rand ($177.3 million), the company said on Wednesday.
Ingwe, controlled by Gencor Ltd, said in a statement on Wednesday that it would acquire the equity in CMAL at a cost of A$88.5 million (310 million rand).
Following the acquisition Ingwe will inject a further A$130 million (490 million rand) to recapitalise the company and allow it to meet future capital expenditure commitments.
Ingwe said that the total cost of the deal would be funded from non-recourse debt and equity. The stake in CMAL was bought from Australian Mutual Provident Society.

"CMAL is a world class asset, which is another step towards fulfilling both Gencor's mission of being a world class natural resources company and Ingwe's mission of being the world's benchmark coal company," Ingwe chairman Mick Davis said.
Ingwe is one of the largest producers of steam coal in the world. In fiscal 1995/96, the company lifted export sales by six percent to 24.5 million tonnes.
CMAL is a medium-sized unlisted coal company with operations in the Newcastle and Hunter coalfields of New South Wales.
Its two main operations are the Bayswater Colliery joint venture and the Wallarah Coal joint venture and production there was expected to exceed 5 million tonnes of coal in 1997.
Davis said CMAL was one of the lowest cost Australian producers and its geographic position would mean distinct advantages in exporting coal to clients in the Far East.

"With the reserves and assets we have acquired with this deal as well as those reserves surrounding CMAL's Wyong and Bayswater reserves, the growth options of this acquisition are formidable," he added.
